ledger.note: 565: the first dated Marquess of Yue, Fu Tan, begins his reign at Kuaiji. The page gives no founding date ('Established: ?'); the ruler table's first reign is 565-538. The disc is the researcher's reading of 'parts of modern Zhejiang'.
482: Yue attacks Wu's capital. Yue 'launched a surprise attack on Wu in 482 BC and conquered the capital'; the Spring and Autumn page: while Fuchai held a conference, Yue captured the Wu capital.

473: the war ends with the annexation of Wu. 'King Goujian destroyed and annexed Wu in 473' (Spring and Autumn page); the Goujian page has the 473 expedition besiege the capital 'for three years before it fell'.

473: Yue moves its court north to the city of Wu. 'After conquering Wu, Yue moved its court north to the city of Wu (modern Suzhou)'; the page gives no year, so 473 is the researcher's bridge.
414: Yue takes Tan. The states table: 'Tan | Tancheng County, Shandong | 414 BCE: to Yue'.

notes: Yue (越; Q1936158). Q1936158 is also on Cliopatria's Minyue row (333-111): the two are DIFFERENT states. Yue is Goujian's kingdom, which ended when Chu (and Qi) partitioned it in 334/333; Minyue is the kingdom its ruling family founded afterwards 'in what is now northern Fujian' (Yue page), with its own dossier (minyue, another part of this group). Yue's successors are Chu, Qi and Minyue. Start 565 is the first dated ruler (Fu Tan, 565-538), not a founding date: the Yue page's 'Established' is '?'. Cliopatria starts the row at 500. Cliopatria problems: its Yue shape is a subset of Wu's shape until 451 (Wu was alive until 473 on the pages); Wu's land goes to Yue in 450, not 473; the shape ends 334, not 333. Pages opened: Yue (state), Goujian (thin), Wu (state), Chu (state), Spring and Autumn period. Not on any page: the Yue capital moves (Kuaiji to Wu has no year; Langya is not mentioned), Zuili 496 and Fujiao 494, the Xuzhou conference, the land Qi ceded in 404, what Chu and Qi each took in 334/333, a 222 Qin conquest of Yue remnants (the Qin dossier cites one with a citation-needed tag). Disagreement: Yue to Chu in 333 (Yue infobox), 334 or 333 (Chu page), 306 (Spring and Autumn table). Gazetteer names wanted: Kuaiji, Gusu, Tan (Tancheng County, Shandong); coordinates used meanwhile.
